kpis.ooo: Too many rooms out of order

occupancy.meaning: Fewer rooms are sold than the budget expects. In an airport hotel the gap is usually on the weekend and the shoulder nights: the weekdays fill themselves with crews and business travellers, Friday to Sunday does not.
moves: Read the weekday averages: open a weekend or leisure rate for the two weakest nights, on the channels that sell at short notice.
Call the airlines and tour operators for crew and layover blocks on the weak nights of the next four weeks.
Compare every morning the rooms on the books with the same weekday last week, and change the rate before the night, not after it.
occupancy.question: Which nights next week are below budget today, and what are we doing about each one?
occupancy.action: Open a rate for the two weakest nights of next week
occupancy.check: Occupancy on those nights reaches the budget four weeks in a row

adr.meaning: The rooms are sold, but cheaper than planned: discounts given at the desk, a group rate on the best nights, or the high-demand nights not priced up.
moves: List the nights above 90% occupancy and check their rates: a sold-out night below the budget ADR is money left on the table.
Close the cheapest rates and the discount channels on nights that fill anyway: fairs, conferences, Tuesday to Thursday.
Agree with the desk which upgrades and discounts they may give, and log every one.
adr.question: On which nights did we sell out below the budget rate, and who decided the rate?
adr.action: Close the discount rates on the nights forecast above 90%
adr.check: ADR on high-demand nights at or above budget for a month

noShows.meaning: More guests than usual do not arrive, and each one is a room that stayed empty on a night it was sold. At an airport the trigger is often outside the house (a strike, cancelled flights), but the guarantee and the release time are inside it.
moves: Check that every reservation arriving after 6 pm has a card guarantee, and charge the no-show fee the same way every night.
Watch the flight board and the airline cancellations in the evening: release unguaranteed rooms early to walk-ins and crews.
Allow a small overbooking on the nights with a high no-show history, agreed with the manager on duty.
noShows.question: Which no-shows of last week were guaranteed, and how many of them did we actually charge?
noShows.action: Charge the guarantee on every no-show and release unguaranteed rooms at 6 pm
noShows.check: No-show rate below 5% of expected arrivals for four weeks

ooo.meaning: A room out of order cannot be sold. A few are normal maintenance; many, or the same rooms for a week, mean a repair is waiting for parts, a decision or a contractor.
moves: List every room out of order with its reason and the date it went out; give each one an owner and a date back in service.
Repair on quiet nights: move planned work to the weekend dip, never into a fair or conference week.
Check with housekeeping every morning which rooms can go back into service today.
ooo.question: Which room has been out of order the longest, and what is it waiting for?
ooo.action: Give every out-of-order room an owner and a date back in service
ooo.check: Out-of-order rooms below 2% of the rooms available for a month

complaints.meaning: More complaints per 100 rooms sold than the house should accept. A complaint is a guest who may not come back, and for every guest who complains there are others who just leave.
moves: Take the complaint causes to Pareto: two causes are usually most of them.
Answer every complaint the same day, with the name of the person who fixed it.
Walk five rooms of the top cause every day this week with housekeeping or maintenance.
complaints.question: What caused most complaints this month, and what did we change because of it?
complaints.action: Fix the top complaint cause and check five rooms a day
complaints.check: Complaints below 2 per 100 rooms sold for a month

onTrack.meaning: Occupancy, ADR, no-shows, out-of-order rooms and complaints are all within budget and limits this month. Keep the routine that got you here.
moves: Read the forecast every morning: the month is not done until its last night is sold.
Look at the weakest weekday and test a rate or a package for it.
Share the result at the morning meeting and name what went well.
onTrack.question: What did we do this month that we should keep doing next month?
onTrack.action: Test a package for the weakest weekday
onTrack.check: The weakest weekday gains five points of occupancy in four weeks

tips: The night audit closes the day: take rooms sold, room revenue and the no-shows from its report before the morning meeting, so the numbers are never more than a day old.
Export the daily statistics from the PMS or the manager's report to Excel and paste the rows. Any date format works, a header row is skipped, and a day pasted twice keeps its latest figures.
A full house at a low rate can earn less than 80% at the budget rate. RevPAR, room revenue per available room, is occupancy and ADR in one number: judge the day by it.
A no-show not charged and a room out of order on a busy night are revenue the house had and lost. The tool prices both at the ADR of that day.
